You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

[
  "Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.",

  "Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.",

]

The redline is position-complete when every element at either the preferred level or the fallback level is met. Do not mark a level complete if an element is omitted, merely promised in the comment, internally inconsistent, or depends on an undefined trigger. Deterministic regexes are evidence; inspect their result in substance as well as mechanically.

Minimal means the proposal changes only what is needed to reach one complete level, retains favourable existing language, avoids duplicating operative terms, and adds no requirement outside the chosen checklist. Treat model-language extras as extras: survival tails, at-own-expense language, additional damages categories, procedures, or boilerplate fail minimality unless a selected element requires them. For a missing clause, a concise insertion can be minimal even though all its words are new. Preserves intent means unrelated allocation, timing, remedies, references, and commercial mechanics survive without contradiction; fail intent if an edit leaves an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained sentence.

Read nouns, modifiers, temporal anchors, amounts, bases, scope, and party direction literally. Do not infer "pro rata" merely from a refund that covers a post-termination period. A no-liquidated-damages result must be unconditional and leave no retained formula, instalment, or contingent payment mechanic. Treat removal of any word outside the chosen elements—even a Customer-favourable restriction—as a minimality failure. Do not infer an omitted element from general commercial context.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

input.summary: Delete Article XXII (Licensor right of first refusal / right to match third-party offers)

The one MFN-family obligation burdening us is Article XXII: we must disclose any bona fide third-party offer for our assets or control and then afford Licensor a right to take that transaction on the same terms — a right-to-match/most-favoured-offer mechanic running in Vendor's favour. It is not limited to a defined product, runs for the entire term (36 months plus extensions, far beyond 12 months) and has no like-for-like comparison carve-outs, so it fails every fallback element and sits in walk-away territory as an open-ended obligation to extend Licensor the terms offered to a third party. We therefore take the preferred position and strike the mechanic, conforming the surviving sentence so no orphan reference to the deleted "Right of First Refusal" or "Exercise Period" remains.

content.text:
Finding submitted.

**MFN — deviation (Article XXII, ¶¶ p0139–p0141).** Pricing (Article V tiers, Supplemental Payments, rebate shares) carries no best-price or best-terms undertaking by us, so the fee mechanics are clean. The responsive burden is the Licensor's Right of First Refusal: we must notify Licensor of any bona fide third-party offer for our assets or control and give Licensor five business days to take that transaction on the same terms — a right-to-match/most-favoured-offer mechanic in Vendor's favour, unlimited as to subject matter, running for the whole term, with no like-for-like comparison carve-outs. It fails all three fallback elements, so we redlined to the preferred position by striking the mechanic and conforming the surviving sentence ("The Licensee shall have the right to consummate the transaction with the third party.") so no orphan reference to the deleted "Right of First Refusal" or "Exercise Period" remains.

messages.content:
Independent verifier feedback follows. Exact unmet checklist text must be repaired in operative language:
Intent defect: restore unrelated commercial language and remove contradictions introduced by the redline.

Verifier reasons:
- Position-complete at the preferred level: the only MFN-family obligation burdening Licensee (the Article XXII disclosure plus right-to-match on a third-party asset sale or change of control) is struck outright, and no Vendor-granted MFN existed that could be lost.
- Minimality is satisfied on the edit itself: only Article XXII's operative mechanic and the conforming lead-in ('In the event the Licensor declines or fails to exercise in full the Right of First Refusal before the expiration of the Exercise Period,') are removed, no survival tails, procedures or extra requirements are added, and the Customer-favourable closing sentence is retained rather than deleted.
- Intent defect — internally inconsistent rendered output: the heading reads 'ARTICLE XXII [INTENTIONALLY OMITTED]' yet operative text ('The Licensee shall have the right to consummate the transaction with the third party.') still follows under it. An article declared intentionally omitted cannot carry a surviving covenant. Repair: either delete the residual sentence with the rest of the article, or move it out from under the omitted heading and restate it as a self-standing provision.
- Intent defect — dangling reference: the retained sentence refers to 'the transaction with the third party' when the deleted text was the only place a third-party offer, asset purchase or merger was described. Repair in operative language, e.g.: 'ARTICLE XXII TRANSFERS. Licensee may sell all or substantially all of its assets, or engage in any merger or consolidation, with any third party without notice to, or any right of first refusal, matching right or consent of, Licensor.'
- Confirm no other article cross-references 'Article XXII', the 'Right of First Refusal' or the 'Exercise Period' (e.g. an assignment, change-of-control or notices provision); the cited extract does not show the rest of the document, and any surviving cross-reference would become orphaned by this deletion.

Re-read any needed source text, validate the revised proposal, rebuild elementCoverage, and submit again.

Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Finding submitted.

**Summary:** ASSIGN is a **deviation** (walk-away territory) in this agreement:

- **Article XXIV(c) (p0149)** flatly prohibits any Licensee assignment or transfer of licence rights without Licensor's consent, with no affiliate or M&A carve-out, and imposes no reciprocal restriction on Licensor — failing even the fallback (no mutual successor-assignment right).
- **Article XX(a) (p0134)** goes further: our Change of Control *automatically terminates* the Agreement and all our licences unless Licensor consents, with Licensor deemed reasonable in refusing on competitive or self-interest grounds.

**Redline (preferred level, three surgical replaces):**
1. Adds a consent-free carve-out for assignment to an Affiliate or an M&A successor, keeping the rest of the sentence and the "void" mechanic verbatim.
2. Replaces the dangling "Section 13.4(a)" change-of-control cross-reference with a Licensor-side restriction: no assignment without our consent (not unreasonably withheld) and never to our competitor.
3. Converts Article XX(a) into an express statement that a Change of Control neither terminates the Agreement nor gives Licensor a termination right, while preserving the "CHANGE OF CONTROL" definition lead-in and Article XX(b).

Noted but not flagged here: Article XXII's right of first refusal on a sale/merger (ROFR/MFN rule) and the separate licence-transfer restrictions in Articles II and VI (IP rule).

Finding rationale:
This sits in walk-away territory on two counts: Article XXIV(c) is a blanket prohibition on Licensee assignment with no affiliate or M&A carve-out and no reciprocal restriction on Licensor, and Article XX(a) automatically terminates the Agreement and all of our licences on our Change of Control unless Licensor consents (with Licensor deemed reasonable in refusing on competitive or self-interest grounds). It therefore fails the fallback (no mutual successor-assignment right) as well as the preferred position. The redline adds our consent-free Affiliate/successor carve-out, subjects Licensor's assignment to our consent (not unreasonably withheld) and bars assignment to our competitors, and removes the change-of-control termination right while leaving the "CHANGE OF CONTROL" definition and Article XX(b) intact. Note separately that the Article XXII right of first refusal on a sale/merger remains and is addressed under the ROFR/MFN rule, not here.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

[
  "Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.",

  "Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.",

]

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee/Customer); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor/Vendor).

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
Position — walk-away:
Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.
Detection guidance:
Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.",
  "The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.",
  "A paid-up licence is perpetual.",
  "A paid-up licence is irrevocable.",
  "A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.",
  "The licence is transferable to Customer's successors."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.",
  "The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction."
]

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee/Customer); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor/Vendor).

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: MFN
Title: Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: MFN in our favour is welcome; an MFN that obliges us to give the Vendor best terms is not.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No MFN obligation on Customer (MFN pricing in Customer's favour is welcome).
Position — fallback:
MFN limited to a defined product, for 12 months, with reasonable-comparison carve-outs.
Position — walk-away:
Open-ended obligation to extend to Vendor any better terms given to any third party.
Detection guidance:
Identify who benefits from the MFN. Flag only when Customer must offer Vendor terms no less favourable than those given to others, or must match third-party offers. If the Vendor grants Customer best pricing, mark compliant and do not redline.

Redline guidance:
Delete the obligation on Customer; keep any Vendor-granted MFN.

Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "The Customer MFN covers only a defined product.",
  "The Customer MFN lasts no longer than 12 months.",
  "The Customer MFN contains reasonable like-for-like comparison carve-outs."
]

input.rationale: The fee articles (Article V user-fee tiers, Supplemental Payments, rebate shares) contain no best-price or best-terms undertaking by Licensee, so pricing is clean. The one MFN-family obligation burdening us is Article XXII: we must disclose any bona fide third-party offer for our assets or control and then afford Licensor a right to take that transaction on the same terms — a right-to-match/most-favoured-offer mechanic running in Vendor's favour. It is not limited to a defined product, runs for the entire term (36 months plus extensions, far beyond 12 months) and has no like-for-like comparison carve-outs, so it fails every fallback element and sits in walk-away territory as an open-ended obligation to extend Licensor the terms offered to a third party. We therefore take the preferred position and strike the mechanic, conforming the surviving sentence so no orphan reference to the deleted "Right of First Refusal" or "Exercise Period" remains.

content.text:
Finding submitted.

**MFN — deviation (Article XXII, ¶¶ p0139–p0141).** Pricing (Article V tiers, Supplemental Payments, rebate shares) carries no best-price or best-terms undertaking by us, so the fee mechanics are clean. The responsive burden is the Licensor's Right of First Refusal: we must notify Licensor of any bona fide third-party offer for our assets or control and give Licensor five business days to take that transaction on the same terms — a right-to-match/most-favoured-offer mechanic in Vendor's favour, unlimited as to subject matter, running for the whole term, with no like-for-like comparison carve-outs. It fails all three fallback elements, so we redlined to the preferred position by striking the mechanic and conforming the surviving sentence ("The Licensee shall have the right to consummate the transaction with the third party.") so no orphan reference to the deleted "Right of First Refusal" or "Exercise Period" remains.

messages.content:
Independent verifier feedback follows. Exact unmet checklist text must be repaired in operative language:
Intent defect: restore unrelated commercial language and remove contradictions introduced by the redline.

Verifier reasons:
- Position-complete at the preferred level: the only MFN-family obligation burdening Licensee (the Article XXII disclosure plus right-to-match on a third-party asset sale or change of control) is struck outright, and no Vendor-granted MFN existed that could be lost.
- Minimality is satisfied on the edit itself: only Article XXII's operative mechanic and the conforming lead-in ('In the event the Licensor declines or fails to exercise in full the Right of First Refusal before the expiration of the Exercise Period,') are removed, no survival tails, procedures or extra requirements are added, and the Customer-favourable closing sentence is retained rather than deleted.
- Intent defect — internally inconsistent rendered output: the heading reads 'ARTICLE XXII [INTENTIONALLY OMITTED]' yet operative text ('The Licensee shall have the right to consummate the transaction with the third party.') still follows under it. An article declared intentionally omitted cannot carry a surviving covenant. Repair: either delete the residual sentence with the rest of the article, or move it out from under the omitted heading and restate it as a self-standing provision.
- Intent defect — dangling reference: the retained sentence refers to 'the transaction with the third party' when the deleted text was the only place a third-party offer, asset purchase or merger was described. Repair in operative language, e.g.: 'ARTICLE XXII TRANSFERS. Licensee may sell all or substantially all of its assets, or engage in any merger or consolidation, with any third party without notice to, or any right of first refusal, matching right or consent of, Licensor.'
- Confirm no other article cross-references 'Article XXII', the 'Right of First Refusal' or the 'Exercise Period' (e.g. an assignment, change-of-control or notices provision); the cited extract does not show the rest of the document, and any surviving cross-reference would become orphaned by this deletion.

Re-read any needed source text, validate the revised proposal, rebuild elementCoverage, and submit again.

input.rationale: The fee articles (Article V user-fee tiers, Supplemental Payments, rebate shares) contain no best-price or best-terms undertaking by Licensee, so pricing is clean. The one MFN-family obligation burdening us is Article XXII: we must disclose any bona fide third-party offer for our assets or control and then afford Licensor five business days to take that transaction on the same terms — a right-to-match/most-favoured-offer mechanic in Vendor's favour. It is not limited to a defined product, runs for the whole term (36 months plus extensions, far beyond 12 months) and has no like-for-like comparison carve-outs, so it fails every fallback element and is walk-away territory. We therefore take the preferred position: the disclosure and matching mechanic is replaced with a short confirmation that no right of first refusal or matching right runs in Licensor's favour, and the surviving Customer-favourable sentence is conformed so Article XXII reads as one self-standing provision with no orphan reference to the deleted "Right of First Refusal" or "Exercise Period" (confirmed those terms and "Article XXII" appear nowhere else). The separate Article XX Change of Control consent regime and Article XXIV(c) assignment consent are left untouched, so nothing outside this rule is disturbed.

content.text:
Resubmitted with the intent defects repaired.

**What changed from the prior version**
- Article XXII no longer reads "[INTENTIONALLY OMITTED]" with a live covenant under it. It now carries a single self-standing provision: *"ARTICLE XXII TRANSFERS Licensee may sell all or substantially all of its assets, or engage in any merger or consolidation, with any third party without notice to, or any right of first refusal or matching right in favor of, Licensor."*
- The dangling reference is cured: the surviving Customer-favourable sentence now reads "The Licensee shall have the right to consummate any such transaction," whose antecedent is the transfer described in the new first sentence.
- Cross-reference check completed: "Right of First Refusal," "Exercise Period" and "Article XXII" appear nowhere else (Article XXIV(c) assignment and Article XX Change of Control cross-refer only to the Change of Control section), so no orphaned references arise.
- Scope discipline: the new sentence negates only the notice/matching mechanic and deliberately does **not** waive consent, so it does not contradict the retained Article XX Change of Control consent regime or the Article XXIV(c) assignment consent (those belong to other rules).

Element coverage: the single preferred element ("Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor") is addressed by operations 1–3; minimality gate returned ok:true.

messages.content:
Independent verifier feedback follows. Exact unmet checklist text must be repaired in operative language:
Minimality defect: revise only the words needed for one complete checklist level and remove extra terms.

Intent defect: restore unrelated commercial language and remove contradictions introduced by the redline.

Verifier reasons:
- Preferred level is complete on its single element: the Article XXII right-of-first-refusal/right-to-match obligation burdening Licensee is removed and expressly negated, and no other Licensee best-terms undertaking exists in the fee articles.
- Minimality fails: the checklist required only deletion of the Customer-side matching obligation. The new sentence goes further by granting Licensee an affirmative right to sell all or substantially all assets or merge with any third party "without notice to" Licensor \u2014 a substantive transfer permission outside the MFN checklist. Repair by limiting the insertion to a negation of the matching right (e.g. "Licensor shall have no right of first refusal or right to match any third-party offer.") or by deleting Article XXII outright.
- Minimality also fails for duplicate operative coverage: the retained sentence "The Licensee shall have the right to consummate any such transaction" now says the same thing as the new first sentence. The retained sentence had meaning only as the tail of the deleted Exercise Period mechanic; it should be struck rather than conformed.
- Preserves intent fails: the drafter expressly leaves Article XX's Change of Control consent regime and Article XXIV(c) assignment consent in place, yet the new Article XXII permits any merger or asset sale "without notice to" Licensor and gives Licensee an unconditional right to consummate. That is a direct contradiction with the retained consent/notice requirements. Repair by (a) removing the "without notice to" and affirmative-permission language, or (b) subordinating the sentence with an express "Subject to Article XX and Article XXIV(c)" qualifier.
- Note also that the deleted defined terms "Right of First Refusal" and "Exercise Period" are confirmed to appear nowhere else, so no dangling cross-reference arises from the deletion itself; the intent defect is the contradiction with the retained change-of-control regime, not an orphan reference.

Re-read any needed source text, validate the revised proposal, rebuild elementCoverage, and submit again.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: Article III is left untouched: "Licensee acknowledges that Licensor owns all right, title, and interest in and to the Licensed Technology and all Intellectual Property Rights therein", and Licensed Technology expressly includes the Licensed Know-How and the Platform Software. Vendor's retained ownership of its own tools/know-how is permitted at the fallback level.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Inserted CUSTOMIZATION DELIVERABLES clause: "Licensor grants Licensee a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license ...", and the grant is expressly stated "Notwithstanding ... the termination of licenses under Article XXI", so Article XXI(a)'s automatic licence termination does not cut it short.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license" with an express override of Article XXI's licence-termination sentence and of the Article II/VI restrictions.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license" — the word "worldwide" appears in the operative grant, and the Article VI field-of-use/territory restrictions are expressly overridden.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense".

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "license to use, modify and sublicense, for Licensee's business, all development and customization work performed for Licensee under Article VII(b)"; the Article III no-copy/no-alter restriction and the Article II restrictions are overridden by the opening "Notwithstanding the foregoing and the restrictions in Articles II and VI".

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "use, modify and sublicense, for Licensee's business" — sublicensing is expressly granted and the retained non-sublicensable/no-reproduction language is overridden.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Second sentence of the insertion: "Any license granted to Licensor in data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Licensee is limited to processing that data solely to provide the services under this Agreement." The trigger covers every category of Customer data (belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Licensee) and no broader Vendor exploitation right survives elsewhere.

elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Article III is retained unchanged and vests all right, title and interest in the Licensed Technology (including Derivative Works comprising the Article VII(b) customizations) in Licensor; the insertion grants only a licence, not ownership.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: No assignment language anywhere in the rendered text; the drafter deliberately chose the licence-back fallback.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Article III preserves Licensor's ownership of the Licensed Technology and its Intellectual Property Rights.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The perpetual licence covers "all development and customization work performed for Licensee under Article VII(b)", which is Licensor-owned IP embedded in those deliverables.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: "perpetual, irrevocable ... license" over the Licensor-owned customization work.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: "royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense".

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: No affirmative sentence stating that Licensee retains all right, title and interest in its data; the insertion only limits any Licensor licence in that data. Note Article XXI(b) still requires Licensee to ship "other Confidential Information" to Licensor on termination without any carve-out for Licensee's own data.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Same sentence as at fallback: any Licensor licence in Licensee data "is limited to processing that data solely to provide the services under this Agreement"; no distribution, resale or "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" language survives.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: No joint-ownership language exists in the cited or rendered text; the condition does not arise, so nothing needs deleting.

reasons: All eight fallback elements are met in operative language: the inserted CUSTOMIZATION DELIVERABLES clause supplies a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the Article VII(b) work for Licensee's business, Vendor's ownership of its platform/know-how is untouched, and any Licensor licence in Licensee data is confined to processing solely to provide the services. The fallback level is position-complete.
Preferred is correctly not claimed: no assignment of the customizations to Licensee and no affirmative Customer Data ownership sentence.

Minimality holds: nothing outside the checklist was deleted or added, no survival tails, expense language or procedures were bolted on, and the narrow "Notwithstanding ... Articles II and VI and the termination of licenses under Article XXI" opener is necessary rather than decorative because the retained Article II/III/VI restrictions (no copying, no modification, field-of-use) and Article XXI(a) would otherwise directly contradict the new grant.

Intent fails on one retained sentence: the override reaches only "the termination of licenses under Article XXI", leaving Article XXI(b) intact, which requires Licensee within five days of termination to "ship to Licensor all Licensed Technology, API's Documentation ... and other Confidential Information in Licensee's possession or control" and to certify compliance by officer. Because the Article VII(b) customizations are Licensor-owned enhancements to the Platform Software (and Derivative Works of the Licensed Technology), the return-and-certify obligation would strip Licensee of every copy of the Customization Deliverables and hollow out the supposedly perpetual and irrevocable licence.

Repair: extend the override to the return and certification obligation, e.g. "Notwithstanding Article XXI(a) and (b), Licensee may retain and continue to use, modify and sublicense the Customization Deliverables (and copies thereof) after termination, and the return and certification obligations in Article XXI(b) shall not apply to the Customization Deliverables or to data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Licensee."

Secondary drafting note (not an element failure): the licence is keyed to "all development and customization work performed for Licensee under Article VII(b)", which is only engaged once a separate written price/scope agreement is signed; consider adding "or under any statement of work or order" so the grant is not left dependent on that single trigger.
