system.text:
You are an independent verifier of one proposed customer-side contract redline in a fresh context.
Treat the preferred and fallback positions as separate atomic checklists. Evaluate the operative rendered language, not the drafter's confidence or margin comment. Copy every supplied element string exactly into the corresponding output item, assess both levels, and return met, not_met, or cannot_tell with concise textual evidence. A conditional element is met when its stated condition does not apply, but explain why.

Apply rule boundaries: voluntary use of one Vendor interface is not a sole-supplier promise when Customer remains free to use alternatives; a disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic is MFN rather than exclusivity unless alternatives remain prohibited after compliance; natural-term non-renewal is evaluated under RENEWAL, not as mid-term T4C; an unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right. An auto-renewal clause permitting either party to terminate on notice does not make Vendor termination term-end-only unless the termination effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. A broad Vendor right to distribute, resell, independently exploit Customer Data, or use it for the wider "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" defeats the solely-to-provide-the-Services element even if ownership nominally remains with Customer. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer remains service delivery. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not itself a standing Vendor licence.

Fail intent if a Customer-only successor or licence-transfer element is implemented by granting Vendor a new assignment exception. A Customer Data insurance trigger must cover every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer, not merely selected named data types. Cosmetic deletion or paraphrase of words outside the target elements fails minimality.

For ASSIGN fallback, any retained no-consent non-successor exception—including a mutual affiliate exception—defeats "Other assignments require consent." Under LICENSE, resolve whether Customer already includes affiliates and fail minimality for duplicate coverage. A grant to an affiliate ordinarily permits use through its authorized personnel; a separate personnel/access edit is unnecessary unless retained language expressly contradicts the new grant. A broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause is non-minimal when a direct "without Vendor approval" transfer permission will do.

The redline is position-complete when every element at either the preferred level or the fallback level is met. Do not mark a level complete if an element is omitted, merely promised in the comment, internally inconsistent, or depends on an undefined trigger. Deterministic regexes are evidence; inspect their result in substance as well as mechanically.

Minimal means the proposal changes only what is needed to reach one complete level, retains favourable existing language, avoids duplicating operative terms, and adds no requirement outside the chosen checklist. Treat model-language extras as extras: survival tails, at-own-expense language, additional damages categories, procedures, or boilerplate fail minimality unless a selected element requires them. For a missing clause, a concise insertion can be minimal even though all its words are new. Preserves intent means unrelated allocation, timing, remedies, references, and commercial mechanics survive without contradiction; fail intent if an edit leaves an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained sentence.

Read nouns, modifiers, temporal anchors, amounts, bases, scope, and party direction literally. Do not infer "pro rata" merely from a refund that covers a post-termination period. Do not equate broader "all amounts paid or payable" with "fees paid or payable", "the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to a claim" with "the 12 months preceding the claim", or a deadline running from a request with one running from termination. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief preserves an otherwise exclusive merits forum; a broader alternate forum does not. A "no field-of-use restriction" result is not complete while an exclusive Vendor right prevents Customer use of its own product or brand. Fail minimality when a fallback proposal exceeds its numeric threshold without necessity. A no-liquidated-damages result must be unconditional and leave no retained formula, instalment, or contingent payment mechanic. Treat removal of any word outside the chosen elements—even a Customer-favourable restriction—as a minimality failure. Do not infer an omitted element from general commercial context.

For a liability cap, resolve the definition used by any Customer-payment carve-out. Language excluding only a narrowly defined subset of Fees does not cover Customer payment obligations as a whole. Treat explanatory examples added to an otherwise complete formula as non-minimal.

For T4C, treat "in whole or in part" as surplus unless the selected checklist and an actual Order Form or partial-termination structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the stated assistance period must apply after every covered expiry or termination; a request condition tied only to anticipated expiry does not suffice. Certified deletion must occur after data return. For WARRANTY fallback, do not treat reports, outputs, or services as software merely because they conform to a manual; require an express software-to-documentation warranty unless the contract defines the item as software.

Give actionable reasons. If an element is not met, name the exact defect the drafter must repair in operative language.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule and exact checklists:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

Finding rationale:
Article III (p0048) vests all right, title and interest in the Licensed Technology and all Intellectual Property Rights therein in Licensor, and "DERIVATIVE WORK" (p0005) sweeps in any additions, modifications, improvements or enhancements. The customization work we commission and pay for under Article VII(b) (p0087) — a unique client front end and other enhancements to the Platform Software — therefore vests entirely in Licensor, while our only right is the non-exclusive Field-of-Use licence that may not be copied, modified or sublicensed (p0042, p0044, p0047, p0048, p0085) and that terminates automatically under Article XXI(a) with a five-day ship-back and officer certification under Article XXI(b) (p0138). That fails the IP fallback: we receive no perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense what we paid for. Licensor's retained ownership of its platform, tools and know-how is acceptable and is left untouched, as are its infringement-enforcement rights, the Article VII(b) pricing mechanic and the balance of Article XXI. No Customer IP or data is assigned to Licensor and there is no standing Licensor licence in our data, so we simply confine any such licence to processing to provide the services. You are in-house counsel producing a concise Markdown issues memo from verified findings.
Include: Executive summary; a Markdown table of findings with severity, rule, status and section; Walk-away items; Next steps.
Never invent a section reference or legal conclusion. Use only supplied findings.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Findings:
[{"id":"f-indemn-52117ca5","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION","rationale":"Indemnity in this Agreement runs one way only: Article XII (p0128-p0129) is a broad Licensee indemnity in favour of Licensor, and there is no Licensor indemnity anywhere (no responsive language in Articles VIII, X, XIII or the General Provisions). Article XIII(a) compounds this by providing that \"UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCE SHALL LICENSOR BE LIABLE FOR ANY ACTIONS, CLAIMS OR THE LIKE ... THAT THE USE OF THE LICENSED TECHNOLOGY ... MAY RESULT IN ANY INFRINGEMENT\", and Article XIII(b) caps Licensor's total liability at one half of amounts paid. That is walk-away territory (no Vendor IP indemnity plus a one-way Customer indemnity), so it fails the fallback. We therefore target the fallback: a Licensor IP indemnity with the customary Customer modification, combination and specification exclusions and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, subject to a 3x annual fees super-cap, and we carve that indemnity out of Article XIII(a) and (b) only so far as necessary to keep it effective. We have not sought the preferred-level additions (defence duty, affiliates, breach of law, data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct, procedure, narrowing of Licensee's indemnity) in this redline.","proposal":"Insert Licensor IP indemnity with customary exclusions, remedies and 3x annual fees super-cap, and conform Article XIII so it does not negate the indemnity.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ip-776e511d","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and agrees that:","rationale":"Article III (p0048) vests all right, title and interest in the Licensed Technology and all Intellectual Property Rights therein in Licensor, and \"DERIVATIVE WORK\" (p0005) sweeps in any additions, modifications, improvements or enhancements. The customization work we commission and pay for under Article VII(b) (p0087) — a unique client front end and other enhancements to the Platform Software — therefore vests entirely in Licensor, while our only right is the non-exclusive Field-of-Use licence that may not be copied, modified or sublicensed (p0042, p0044, p0047, p0048, p0085) and that terminates automatically under Article XXI(a) with a five-day ship-back and officer certification under Article XXI(b) (p0138). That fails the IP fallback: we receive no perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense what we paid for. Licensor's retained ownership of its platform, tools and know-how is acceptable and is left untouched, as are its infringement-enforcement rights, the Article VII(b) pricing mechanic and the balance of Article XXI. No Customer IP or data is assigned to Licensor and there is no standing Licensor licence in our data, so we simply confine any such licence to processing to provide the services. We drafted to the fallback rather than the preferred level (no assignment of the customizations to us and no affirmative data-ownership sentence) to avoid collateral rewrites of Articles II, III, VI and XXI; the named override of Article III and Article XXI(a) and (b) is the minimum needed to keep the perpetual licence from being cancelled or surrendered.","proposal":"Add a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the Article VII(b) customization work for our business, and limit any Licensor licence in our data to processing to provide the services.","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-lol-cap-b6210253","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION","rationale":"Article XIII is the only cap in the Agreement (no other \"aggregate liability\" or \"exceed\" language exists). It caps Licensor alone at one half of amounts paid, leaving Licensee's liability wholly uncapped — and Licensee additionally bears a broad indemnity in Article XII. That is walk-away territory on two counts (one-sided cap; Vendor cap effectively below 6 months' fees) and there are no carve-outs for indemnity, confidentiality, gross negligence or willful misconduct (the gross negligence/willful misconduct reference in Article II is an exception to Licensee's assumption of risk, not a cap carve-out). We target the fallback: cap made mutual at 12 months' fees plus the four fallback carve-outs, in two surgical edits. We deliberately did not make the Article XIII(a) consequential-damages waiver mutual (it currently protects only Licensor, so Customer benefits from the asymmetry) and note, without redlining, that Licensor's blanket exclusion of IP-infringement liability in (a) and the absence of a USD 1,000,000 floor fall short of our preferred position.","proposal":"Make the liability cap mutual at 12 months' fees and place indemnity, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct outside the cap.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-assign-d6b135ce","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"GENERAL PROVISIONS","rationale":"This sits in walk-away territory on two counts: Article XXIV(c) is a blanket prohibition on Licensee assignment with no affiliate or M&A carve-out and no reciprocal restriction on Licensor, and Article XX(a) automatically terminates the Agreement and all of our licences on our Change of Control unless Licensor consents (with Licensor deemed reasonable in refusing on competitive or self-interest grounds). It therefore fails the fallback as well as the preferred position. The redline adds our consent-free Affiliate/successor carve-out, adds a short Licensor-side restriction (our consent, not unreasonably withheld, and never to a competitor of ours), and removes the change-of-control termination right while leaving the \"CHANGE OF CONTROL\" definition and Article XX(b) intact. The Customer-favourable routing sentence keeping a Change of Control outside the assignment-consent prohibition is retained verbatim. The Article XXII right of first refusal on a sale/merger remains and is addressed under the ROFR/MFN rule, not here.","proposal":"Add Licensee affiliate/successor assignment carve-out, add a Licensor assignment restriction, and remove automatic termination on Licensee change of control.","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-exclusivity-fd61d096","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and agrees that:","rationale":"The Agreement imposes no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on us, so it meets the preferred position. The licence is expressly non-exclusive and runs in Vendor's favour (Licensor may license the technology to others), which is not a restriction on Customer. There is no requirements commitment, minimum volume routed to the Platform, or prohibition on procuring FX platform services from third parties; the fee provisions (p0070, p0078) only price usage of the Licensed Technology and its third-party revenue. The Article XXII Right of First Refusal (p0139–p0141) is a change-of-control first-look on a sale or merger of Licensee, and once the Exercise Period lapses \"Licensee shall have the right to consummate the transaction with the third party\" — a right-to-match mechanic, not exclusive dealing. The Field of Use definition and the anti-redistribution covenants (p0007, p0027, p0041, p0085) limit how we may use Vendor's technology rather than where we may source competing services; those are licence-scope and IP issues, not exclusivity. No redline proposed under this rule.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ld-b5abca07","ruleId":"LD","ruleTitle":"Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION","rationale":"The Agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, stipulated-sum or minimum/early-termination fee payable by Licensee. The fee architecture (Articles IV, V and VII, paragraphs p0049-p0089) is purely usage-based (per US$1m traded), plus a fixed $2,500/month support charge, with no committed volume, shortfall/true-up or post-termination minimum; Article XXI (p0138) imposes only return of materials on termination, and Article XXIII (p0142) expressly bars termination damages of any kind against either party. The only cost-shifting mechanics that touch Licensee are ordinary and not liquidated amounts: the audit-cost shift if a discrepancy exceeds 5% (p0064) and the fee-calculation floor tied to actual recorded volume (p0070), neither of which is a stipulated damages amount. Licensor's immediate-termination right on breach (p0049) preserves only payment for trades actually performed, i.e. accrued fees. This meets the preferred position (Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties), so no redline is warranted; we would only revisit if a renewal or amendment introduced a committed-volume shortfall charge.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-license-419e22df","ruleId":"LICENSE","ruleTitle":"Licence grant scope","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and agrees that:","rationale":"The grant in Article II runs to Licensee alone, and the restrictions bar access by any individuals other than Licensee's own employees (p0045) and any transfer of licence rights without consent (p0042, p0149). There is no path to add Affiliates, and Article XX (p0134) automatically terminates the Agreement and all licences on any Change of Control unless Licensor consents, with consent deemed reasonably withheld on broad grounds — so the licence is not transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition. Both fallback elements fail on their material terms. We have taken the fallback: Affiliates (and their personnel, deemed Licensee employees so the existing use restrictions do not defeat the grant) are covered on written notice, and the change-of-control mechanic is conformed so the licence continues and transfers to our successor in a merger or acquisition without Licensor's approval; the assignment clause already defers Change of Control to that section, so no further edit is needed. Preferred items (perpetual/irrevocable paid-up licence, contractors, termination only for uncured material breach) are not pursued at this level.","proposal":"Extend licence to Affiliates on written notice and permit transfer to a successor in a merger or acquisition","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-noncompete-2c845a87","ruleId":"NONCOMPETE","ruleTitle":"Non-compete restrictions on Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION","rationale":"We traced every restriction-bearing provision (Article II licence restrictions and Additional Restrictions at p0027, p0030, p0040-p0047; Article VI sub-licence bar at p0085; the restrictive-covenants article at p0124-p0125; the Change of Control and Right of First Refusal articles at p0134 and p0139; and General Provisions at p0144-p0159). None restricts the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build: the only restrictive covenant binding us is an employee non-solicit (a NONSOLICIT matter, not flagged here), and we are nowhere barred from using, buying or building competing FX platforms or from competing with Licensor. The \"Field of Use\" limit (p0007, p0030) and the Derivative Work / distribution bars (p0044, p0085) are scope limits on our use of Licensor's own Licensed Technology, not a field-of-use restraint on our business, and the licence is expressly non-exclusive in both directions (p0043), so Licensor holds no exclusive right preventing us from using or licensing our own product or brand. The Change of Control consent mechanic keyed to a competitive acquirer (p0134) is a change-of-control/assignment term addressed under that rule and is not double-flagged here. The rule's preferred position - no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer - is therefore met.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-renewal-b8bf2ee0","ruleId":"RENEWAL","ruleTitle":"Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and agrees that:","rationale":"Article IV(I) lets Licensor unilaterally extend the Agreement for an additional seven years at its own option. Customer has no non-renewal notice window at all and would be locked into a multi-year extension it never agreed to, which is walk-away territory under this rule (automatic multi-year renewals) and fails the fallback (non-renewal window of no more than 60 days). The clause also conflicts with Article IV(II)-(III), which contemplate extension only by mutual written agreement. The shortest cure is to make renewal mutual, matching the preferred position's first limb; no price-escalation mechanic exists anywhere in the fee provisions (Article V), so no uplift cap is needed once renewal is mutual.","proposal":"Renewal only by mutual written agreement instead of Licensor's unilateral 7-year extension option","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-t4c-0c664744","ruleId":"T4C","ruleTitle":"Termination for convenience","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and agrees that:","rationale":"The Term article commits us to a 36-month Initial Period and no provision anywhere gives Licensee any right to terminate without cause: Licensor's termination rights are cause-based (breach under Article IV and Article II, insolvency under Article XIX, wind-up/change of control under Article XX), and there is no refund mechanic at all. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a multi-year term is walk-away territory under T4C and fails the fallback, which requires at least a 60-90 day Customer exit. We therefore added the shortest preferred-level clause: 30 days' notice, pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and express confirmation that Licensor has no convenience right during the term. Licensor's 7-year unilateral renewal option is a RENEWAL issue and is not flagged here.","proposal":"Add a Licensee termination-for-convenience right on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and confirm Licensor has no convenience right during the term.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-audit-052b44a8","ruleId":"AUDIT","ruleTitle":"Audit rights against Customer","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"50+ US$5.00","rationale":"The only audit right binding us is Article V.IV(b) (p0073), with cost allocation in p0064. It uses an independent CPA/audit professional and puts cost on Licensor unless a discrepancy exceeds 5%, which already matches the preferred cost and auditor elements. However, it contains no frequency limit (audits could be demanded repeatedly), no prior-notice requirement (the 30-day window is a deadline for us to permit the audit, not notice to us), and no business-hours, confidentiality, off-site or system-access protections. Unlimited audits on no notice is walk-away territory and fails the fallback (once per year on 15 days' notice), so we have added the missing guardrails at the preferred level with two short edits, leaving the auditor-selection and 5% cost-shift terms untouched.","proposal":"Add frequency, notice, business-hours, confidentiality, off-site and no-system-access limits to the Licensor audit right","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-govlaw-ceb82bf3","ruleId":"GOVLAW","ruleTitle":"Governing law and venue","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"GENERAL PROVISIONS","rationale":"Article XXIV(a) selects New York internal law, and the following paragraph requires any suit arising out of or relating to the Agreement to be instituted in the City of New York with irrevocable submission to the exclusive jurisdiction of the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York or any New York State court, plus a venue/forum non conveniens waiver. {"markdown":"# Issues Memo — FX Platform Licence Agreement

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Verified playbook findings and redline positions 
**Comment prefix in redline:** `[Playbook]`

---

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against the playbook and verified 18 findings: **13 deviations or gaps** (three of them critical) and **five compliant clauses**. The risk profile is heavily one-sided.

The critical cluster concerns risk allocation and ownership. Indemnity runs one way only — Article XII is a broad Licensee indemnity in favour of Licensor, with no Licensor indemnity anywhere, and Article XIII(a) expressly disclaims Licensor liability for infringement while Article XIII(b) caps Licensor at one half of amounts paid. The same Article XIII is the only cap in the Agreement, leaving our liability wholly uncapped with no carve-outs. On IP, Article III vests all right, title and interest in Licensor, and the "Derivative Work" definition sweeps in the customization work we commission and pay for under Article VII(b), leaving us with only a terminable non-exclusive Field-of-Use licence.

The high-severity cluster concerns our ability to stay in and to get out: no Licensee termination-for-convenience right in a 36-month term; a unilateral Licensor option to extend for a further seven years; a blanket bar on Licensee assignment coupled with automatic termination on our change of control; and a licence grant that reaches neither our Affiliates nor a successor. Medium items include an unlimited, no-notice audit right, a three-year one-way non-solicit covering all Vendor personnel, an Article XXII right of first refusal on a sale or merger of Licensee, an "AS IS" disclaimer with no affirmative warranty, and no post-termination transition assistance or data return.

On the positive side, exclusivity, non-compete, minimum-commitment, liquidated-damages and governing-law provisions all meet our preferred position and require no redline. Pricing is usage-based and clean of best-price undertakings.

---

## Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Position / proposal |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION | Insert Licensor IP indemnity with customary exclusions, remedies and 3x annual fees super-cap, and conform Article XIII so it does not negate the indemnity. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and agrees that: | Add a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the Article VII(b) customization work, and limit any Licensor licence in our data to processing to provide the services. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION | Make the cap mutual at 12 months' fees and place indemnity, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct outside the cap. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | GENERAL PROVISIONS | Add Licensee affiliate/successor carve-out, add a Licensor-side assignment restriction, and remove automatic termination on Licensee change of control. |
| 5 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and agrees that: | Extend the licence to Affiliates on written notice and permit transfer to a successor in a merger or acquisition. |
| 6 | High | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | Deviation | § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and agrees that: | Renewal only by mutual written agreement, in place of Licensor's unilateral seven-year extension option. |
| 7 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and agrees that: | Add a Licensee convenience right on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; confirm Licensor has no convenience right during the term. |
| 8 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and agrees that: | No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on us; meets preferred position. No redline. |
| 9 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION | No liquidated damages, penalty or minimum/early-termination fee; fees are usage-based. No redline. |
| 10 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION | No restriction on the businesses we operate or the products we buy or build; meets preferred position. No redline. |
| 11 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | 50+ US$5.00 | Add frequency, notice, business-hours, confidentiality, off-site and no-system-access limits; leave auditor selection and the 5% cost shift untouched. |
| 12 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Deviation | CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION | Strike Article XXII's right-of-first-refusal mechanic and its tail sentence, leaving only a negation of the matching right. |
| 13 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Deviation | CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION | Narrow the one-way three-year non-solicit to a mutual 12-month restriction limited to personnel directly involved in the services. |
| 14 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | WARRANTY DISCLAIMER | Add express software/services warranty with repair, replacement or refund remedy and carve it out of the "AS IS" disclaimer. |
| 15 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION | Insert transition assistance and Licensee Data return/deletion obligations in Article XXI. |
| 16 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | GENERAL PROVISIONS | New York law; exclusive New York state and federal courts; no arbitration. Meets preferred position. No redline. |
| 17 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and agrees that: | No minimum, take-or-pay or shortfall mechanic; volume band starts at zero. No redline. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | GENERAL PROVISIONS | Insert a short insurance covenant (E&O USD 1M; cyber/privacy USD 2M) in General Provisions. |

---

## Walk-away items

The following findings sit in walk-away territory under the playbook and, in our view, cannot be signed as drafted:

1. **INDEMN** — No Vendor IP indemnity anywhere, combined with a one-way Licensee indemnity in Article XII and an express Licensor disclaimer of infringement liability in Article XIII(a). Fallback ask: Licensor IP indemnity with modification/combination/specification exclusions and procure–modify–replace–refund remedies, subject to a 3x annual fees super-cap, carved out of Article XIII(a) and (b) only so far as necessary.
2. **LOL-CAP** — One-sided cap; Licensor capped at one half of amounts paid (effectively below six months' fees) with Licensee uncapped and no carve-outs. Fallback ask: mutual 12-month cap plus the four carve-outs.
3. **ASSIGN** — Blanket bar on Licensee assignment with no affiliate or M&A carve-out and no reciprocal Licensor restriction, plus automatic termination of all licences on our change of control under Article XX(a).
4. **RENEWAL** — Licensor's unilateral seven-year extension option with no non-renewal window for us.
5. **T4C** — No Licensee convenience right at all in a 36-month Initial Period, and no refund mechanic.
6. **AUDIT** — Unlimited audits on no prior notice, with no business-hours, confidentiality or system-access protections.
7. **MFN** — Article XXII right to match any third-party offer for our assets or control, unlimited in scope and running for the whole term.
8. **NOSOLICIT** — One-way 36-month non-solicit reaching all Licensor and Affiliate personnel.
9. **TRANSITION** — Our licences end immediately with a five-day ship-back and officer's certificate, and nothing obliges Licensor to return or export our data.
10. **WARRANTY** — Pure "AS IS" supply with an express disclaimer that nonconformity to Documentation will be corrected.
11. **INSURANCE** — No coverage covenant at all, where Licensor hosts the platform and receives our market data and trading orders.

**Also below fallback (not walk-away):** IP ownership of the Article VII(b) customizations we pay for, and the licence grant's failure to reach our Affiliates or a successor.

---

## Next steps

1. **Confirm the walk-away list with the business.** We should agree internally, before the first exchange, that items 1–3 above (indemnity, liability cap, change-of-control/assignment) are signature conditions.
2. **Issue the redline in one pass**, drafted to the fallback where noted (indemnity, liability cap, licence scope, non-solicit) and to the preferred position where the fallback edit is no shorter (audit guardrails, MFN deletion, transition, termination for convenience).
3. **Sequence the negotiation** around the three critical items; the medium items (audit, non-solicit, warranty, transition, insurance) are drafted as short surgical edits and should be presented as a package for acceptance rather than clause-by-clause debate.
4. **Hold the identified fallbacks in reserve:** 90-day transition assistance with 30-day data export; 12-month mutual non-solicit; annual audit on 15 days' notice.
5. **Flag two drafting points for correction on the technical pass**, not as issues: the reference in the fee-calculation provision to amounts payable by "the Licensor" (evidently intended as Licensee), and the conflict between Licensor's unilateral extension option and the Term provisions contemplating extension only by mutual written agreement.
6. **Re-run verification** after Vendor's markup; three findings were repaired in this cycle (IP, ASSIGN, MFN, NOSOLICIT) and should be re-checked for orphaned cross-references."}
